account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI day-2 post-earnings continuation - the forced spec EXPIRED UNFILLED at 10:30, and the cost of the miss has now given five different answers in five hours
entryWatch.trigger: DEAD. The 6-share buy at a 39.64 limit expired unfilled at 10:30 and the broker returns ZERO equity orders in this account today. SMCI is 39.65 bid / 39.66 ask at 14:21 - +5.42% on the day and 0.03% above the dead limit - so a fill would now be +0.06 unrealized on 237.84, against +12.36 at 11:21, +1.38 at 12:21 and +2.70 at 13:21. Struck at the open: bid 39.61 / ask 39.64 at 13:46:16 UTC.
entryWatch.why: ONE DEAD LIMIT, FIVE HOURLY GRADES, AND THE PRICE HAS NOW RETURNED TO WITHIN THREE CENTS OF WHERE IT LAPSED. The phantom position has read +12.36, +1.38, +2.70 and +0.06 across four consecutive hours on a decision that was made once, at 10:21, and has not changed since. The 11:21 entry led with the number that embarrassed this board because the 10:21 entry had cited the 8/10 JOBY spec as precedent that a lapsed limit costs nothing; the 12:21 entry led with the fact that 89% of that cost had evaporated; the 13:21 entry added a fourth reading and stopped drawing a lesson from any single one. This entry adds the fifth and closes the argument: the price is back to the limit, so the entire eleven-dollar span of verdicts resolved to approximately nothing. THE MEASUREMENT FINDING IS NOW DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS SLOT HAS PRODUCED TODAY. An identical decision graded at five consecutive hours produced five different verdicts, and the final one is indistinguishable from the first. None of them was ever evidence about whether declining to re-strike was correct. A board that had let any single hour settle the question would have recorded a conclusion the next hour erased, and the only defensible verdict belongs to the week's close rather than to any hour inside it. THE SPEC IS STILL NOT RE-STRUCK, AND 39.65 IS THE HARDEST VERSION OF THAT REFUSAL SO FAR. The price is three cents above the dead limit: re-striking here would cost essentially nothing against the original entry, which is exactly why the reason has to be the rulebook rather than the price. It is the same forced item-2 failure at 39.65 that it was at 41.70, 25.5% above the pre-print 31.60 close, on a name whose two-session tape still holds no day-2/3 pullback that has actually happened. A round trip from 39.64 up to 41.70 and back inside one session is an extension breathing, not the multi-session pullback the rulebook names. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text, was discharged for 2026-08-13, and this slot's default is no trade with an explicitly HIGHER bar. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT, UNCHANGED FROM 11:21, 12:21 AND 13:21 SO THE GRADER CAN CHECK IT: a genuine day-2/3 pullback that holds, bought there rather than here. It has not appeared, and no limit was placed below the market to pretend otherwise.

entryWatch.setup: Options are available for the first time - the standing spread refusal was about the names, not the instrument
entryWatch.trigger: SMCI 2026-09-18 calls, live chain: the 40 strike bid 3.75 / ask 3.95, a 5.19% spread on 14,793 open interest and 0.544 delta. The 38 reads 4.21% and the 39 reads 5.85%.
entryWatch.why: A CLAIM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED SINCE 8/5 IS RETIRED, AND IT WAS ALWAYS NARROWER THAN IT SOUNDED. Options were refused three-plus sessions running on spread - most recently at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, on the tightest of eight live quotes - and docs/RULES.md records the finding as 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks'. What the universe actually was: SOUN, SMR and UPST, three small low-priced names, quoted at 15-45% of mark. The first genuinely liquid chain this board has pulled clears the ceiling on all three strikes examined, at 36 days to expiry and 0.54-0.63 delta. So the correct statement is that the names this account could afford had unusable option markets, not that options are unusable at this account size - and the 8/10 note that 'no balance narrows a spread' is true and was answering a question nobody should have been asking. THE CONTRACT WAS STILL NOT BOUGHT, ON ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ON THE OLD REFUSAL. One 40-strike contract at the 3.85 mark is 385.00, 38.0% of a 1012.33 account against a 40% ceiling, and the rulebook's -40% option stop puts 154.00 at risk - 15.2% of the account - behind a thesis this run has itself marked forced. Theta -0.0556 a day takes about 10% of premium over five flat sessions and vega 0.0496 against a still-elevated 78.5% post-print IV takes about 17% more on a 13-point decay, so the contract can lose a quarter of its value while the thesis is neither right nor wrong. The 6-share equity risks 19.03 at its stop and loses only on direction. THIS ROW IS THE FINDING AND NOT A PLAN. The next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced, the option is genuinely on the table for the first time; recorded now so that decision is made against a quoted precedent rather than against a rule of thumb nobody re-tested.

entryWatch.setup: Breadth is 11 green of 12 and the entry is being taken into it - stated as a caution, not a tailwind
entryWatch.trigger: No level. 11 green of 12 on the bid at 09:46, LEU alone red at -0.12%, with the range running SMCI +5.32% down to JOBY +0.13%.
entryWatch.why: ITEM 2's SECOND SENTENCE IS THE ONE THAT APPLIES HERE AND IT IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS RUN'S OWN ENTRY. 'If the whole list is green 5-10%, that is a wait signal, not a buy signal.' The list is not green 5-10% - the magnitudes run +0.13% to +5.32% and only SMCI is above 4% - so the sentence does not fire on its terms, and this row says so rather than stretching it into a refusal it does not support. What IS true and is worth more than the letter of the rule: on a tape where eleven of twelve names are up, most of any one name's move is the tape, and the part of SMCI's +5.32% that belongs to SMCI is smaller than it looks at 09:46. That is the argument for the catalyst having to carry the position rather than the momentum, and it is the argument for the -8% stop being tight against a name whose own session range is already 4.2% wide. Both are written down before the outcome. THE COMPLEX PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND UNCROWDED. OKLO holds one nuclear slot; SMR at +1.67% and LEU at -0.12% could take the second and neither has a catalyst. The SMCI entry is ai-hardware, a complex this book has never held, so the two-per-complex cap is nowhere near binding and no stop in this book gaps with another. AMD at a 496.00 bid is the only other ai-hardware name on the list and is refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% ceiling, which also means the complex cannot accidentally fill from that direction. THE DEAD JOBY SPECIFICATION IS RETIRED FROM THIS FILE. The forced 8.85 limit expired unfilled on 8/10; JOBY is 7.97 bid, -9.94% against it, and has been red against that limit at every one of thirteen reads since. The point is made and re-marking it a fourteenth time adds nothing.
